newsitem.title: INDONESIA: List of suitors for Indonesia Astra grows.
newsitem.headline: List of suitors for Indonesia Astra grows.

text.p: The list of suitors for Indonesia's Astra International appeared to be growing on Friday as a newspaper reported that President Suharto's eldest daughter was in talks to buy out the firm's largest shareholder.

Bisnis Indonesia daily quoted an unnamed source as saying Suharto's daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana, head of toll-road operator Citra Marga, had talks on Thursday with plantations magnate Prajogo Pangestu for his 10.68 percent stake in Astra. Aides of Rukmana and Pangestu refused to comment.

The daily also said a group with links to Suharto and his eldest son was holding separate talks to buy Astra shares from a tobacco tycoon and would approach state banks and government pension funds for their stakes in the blue-chip vehicle maker.

Shares of Astra began rising at the beginning of last week on rumours that a takeover bid was in progress and brokers have said some 100 million shares, or about 10 percent of the company's equity, have since changed hands. The share closed at 3,775 rupiah on Friday, up from 2,625 on September 16.
Businessman Putera Sampoerna, who controls cigarette company Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, said earlier in the week he had bought some shares in Astra but declined to say how many.
Bisnis Indonesia said the Nusamba group, controlled by timber tycoon Muhammad (Bob) Hasan, was seeking to buy Sampoerna's share holdings in Astra.

Hasan is a close associate of Suharto and Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations controlled by the president. Hasan owns 10 percent and the president's eldest son Sigit Hardjojudanto owns the rest.
Spokeswomen for Sampoerna and Hasan also refused comment.
Brokers said that despite the lack of confirmation there was growing certainty that the Suharto family was buying into Astra.

"The first family seems interested in acquiring a stake in Astra," said the research head of a foreign brokerage, adding that Rukmana, Suharto's second son Bambang Trihatmodjo and youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra were all prospective buyers.

Mandala Putra is the sole beneficiary of Indonesia's controversial national car policy, which grants his joint venture with South Korea's Kia Motors tax and tariff breaks on the condition that local content requirements are met within three years.
Trihatmodjo, the head of the Bimantara group, has set up an automobile joint venture with Hyundai Motor Co, South Korea's largest car manufacturer.
The brokerage research head said Astra would be an attractive prospect for all three siblings but added that Mandala Putra was most in need of a production and distribution base for his Timor sedan.

"Buying now is being done by people who are friends of the first family or by those trying to make a profit," said another foreign broker. "Sampoerna is unlikely to want to get into the automobile industry, he just wants to make some cash gains."
Astra's holdings are widely scattered and brokers have said a stake of around 20 would be enough to gain control.
But Astra is owned 8.26 percent by Toyota Motor Co and brokers have said it is unlikely that the Japanese firm will look kindly upon even indirect links with South Korean rivals.
A Toyota spokesman in Tokyo said only: "Our relationship with Astra is solid and will not be broken easily."
